parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: The warranty-disclaimer block (Article VIX and the all-caps paragraphs) is the usual home for a consequential-damages exclusion and cap; check Article X and General Provisions for a monetary cap. Expect a one-sided Licensor-favouring exclusion with no mutual cap and no carve-outs for IP infringement, confidentiality breach or willful misconduct.

No indemnity heading appears in the outline; scan Article X, the confidentiality article and General Provisions for any hidden hold-harmless language. If truly absent, propose a Licensor IP-infringement and misconduct indemnity, and resist any reverse indemnity attached to the licence restrictions in Article II.

Article II licence restrictions and the 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' article are the likely sources of restraints on our business (e.g., bars on competing FX platforms or building similar software). Also check the FIELD OF USE definition in Article I for an indirect non-compete.

The defined terms 'Right of First Refusal' and 'FIELD OF USE' signal exclusivity mechanics; trace where Right of First Refusal is used (likely Article VIII with the pricing tiers) to see whether we are barred from sourcing another FX platform.

Check the per-Market-Day pricing tiers and the Supplemental Payments / Right of First Refusal definitions for any obligation that we offer Licensor terms no worse than those given to others; MFN running in our favour is acceptable, the reverse is not.

The 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' article (Article X) is the direct hit. Confirm mutuality, a term no longer than 12 months post-termination, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Term and termination likely sit in Article VIII (see 'Initial Period' definition) with possible clean-up in General Provisions. Look for a Customer convenience right on notice without penalty and delete any Licensor right to terminate at will or accelerate Supplemental Payments.
Tied to 'Initial Period'; check for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window (we want no more than 30 days) and any uncapped price uplift on renewal against the tiered rates.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause should be in Article XXIV / GENERAL PROVISIONS. Verify New York (or another accepted jurisdiction) and courts rather than offshore arbitration; also check for jury-trial waiver and fee-shifting.

Assignment is almost certainly in General Provisions (Article XXIV). We need affiliate/successor assignment without consent; strike any Licensor termination right on our change of control and check the AFFILIATE definition supports it.

Definitions of DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, MORAL RIGHTS and LICENSED TECHNOLOGY plus the Article II grant/restrictions will allocate ownership. Ensure our data, configurations and any feedback or customer-funded work do not vest in Licensor and that we retain rights in our trading data.

Article II is the grant. Confirm the licence extends to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, is non-revocable during the term (not 'revocable at will'), and that FIELD OF USE / PLATFORM SOFTWARE scope is broad enough for our intended use.

Usage-verification rights typically ride with the Article II restrictions or the per-Market-Day fee reporting in Article VIII. Seek annual frequency, prior written notice, business-hours/remote-first access and Licensor bearing its own costs.

No damages/penalty heading appears; check the fee and Supplemental Payments provisions in Article VIII for late-payment interest, accelerated fees or stipulated damages payable by us, and confirm no service credits exist that we should be asking for.

Article VIX is a pure WARRANTY DISCLAIMER (including express disclaimer that defects will be corrected). We need an affirmative performance/conformity-to-Documentation warranty with a repair-or-refund remedy carved out of the disclaimer.

No insurance article in the outline. Given Licensor hosts the Platform and touches our trading and client data, propose commercial general liability, tech E&O/cyber and, if personnel are on site, workers' compensation, with certificates on request.

The tiered per-unit rates (US$7.50 down to US$5.00) and 'Supplemental Payments' / 'Market Day' definitions suggest volume-based or minimum commitments. Check for take-or-pay minimums, shortfall true-ups or exclusivity-linked volumes, and secure an exit or downward adjustment.

No wind-down or data-return provision is visible; the post-termination effects paragraphs in Article VIII and the confidentiality return-of-materials language are the places to check. If absent, add transition assistance at then-current rates plus return/deletion of our data in a usable format.
